```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 300, dev = "ragg_png",
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table); library(ggplot2); library(flextable); library(officer); library(officedown)
})
for (f in list.files("R", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
flextable_style()

fig_dir <- file.path(params$out_dir, "figures"); tab_dir <- file.path(params$out_dir, "tables")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE); dir.create(tab_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
save_fig <- function(p, name, width = 6.5, height = 4) {
  ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 300,
         device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white")
  p
}
# invisible(): a visible return value would be printed into the Word document.
save_tab <- function(df, name) { fwrite(df, file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".csv"))); invisible(df) }

h <- load_harmonised(params$data_dir)
d <- h$d; R <- h$rounds
cfg_rounds <- fread(file.path(params$config_dir, "rounds.csv"))
design <- make_design(d, params$cluster)
lab <- function(id) R$round_lab[match(id, R$round_id)]
unweighted <- R[weighted == FALSE, round]

# ---- national estimates --------------------------------------------------
fcs_nat <- dcast(as.data.table(estimate_by(design, c("FCS", "fcs_poor", "fcs_border", "fcs_accept", "fcs_pb", "fcs_pb21"))),
                 round_id ~ var, value.var = c("est", "lo", "hi"))
rcsi_nat <- dcast(as.data.table(estimate_by(design, c("rCSI", "rcsi_p1", "rcsi_p2", "rcsi_p3"))),
                  round_id ~ var, value.var = c("est", "lo", "hi"))
both_nat <- as.data.table(estimate_by(design, "both_severe"))
lcs_nat <- dcast(as.data.table(estimate_by(design, c("lcs_none", "lcs_stress", "lcs_crisis", "lcs_emergency", "lcs_ce", "lcs_ce_round"))),
                 round_id ~ var, value.var = c("est", "lo", "hi"))
lcs_nat <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round, round_lab, season, year, weighted)], lcs_nat, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
# HHS is collected from Oct 2019: estimate on the rounds where it exists.
hhs_design <- subset(design, !is.na(HHS))
hhs_nat <- dcast(as.data.table(estimate_by(hhs_design, c("HHS", "hhs_moderate", "hhs_severe", "hhs_p3", paste0("hhs_ph", 1:5)))),
                 round_id ~ var, value.var = c("est", "lo", "hi"))
hhs_nat <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round, round_lab, season, year, weighted)], hhs_nat, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
hhs_first_oct <- hhs_nat[season == "Oct", round_id][1]
hdds_nat <- dcast(as.data.table(estimate_by(design, c("HDDS", "hdds_p3", paste0("hdds_ph", 1:5)))),
                  round_id ~ var, value.var = c("est", "lo", "hi"))
hdds_nat <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round, round_lab, season, year, weighted)], hdds_nat, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
fcs_nat <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round, round_lab, season, year, weighted)], fcs_nat, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
rcsi_nat <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round, round_lab, season, year, weighted)], rcsi_nat, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]

# ---- rounds used for regional comparisons ---------------------------------
oct_w <- R[season == "Oct" & weighted == TRUE, round_id]
latest <- tail(oct_w, 1); previous <- tail(head(oct_w, -1), 1)
first_oct <- R[season == "Oct", round_id][1]; last_oct <- tail(R[season == "Oct", round_id], 1)
first_feb <- R[season == "Feb", round_id][1]; last_feb <- tail(R[season == "Feb", round_id], 1)

region_est <- function(var, rid) {
  x <- as.data.table(estimate_by(subset(design, round_id == rid), var, by = ~admin1))
  n <- d[round_id == rid, .N, by = admin1]
  x <- merge(x, n, by = "admin1")
  x[N < params$min_cell, c("est", "lo", "hi") := NA_real_]
  x
}
g <- function(dt, col, rid) dt[round_id == rid][[col]]
```

# Key messages

```{r key-messages}
pb <- function(rid) g(fcs_nat, "est_fcs_pb", rid)
p3 <- function(rid) g(rcsi_nat, "est_rcsi_p3", rid)
dir_word <- function(a, b) if (b > a + 0.01) "rose" else if (b < a - 0.01) "fell" else "remained stable"
oct_pb <- fcs_nat[season == "Oct"]; peak_oct <- oct_pb[which.max(est_fcs_pb)]
reg_fcs_latest <- region_est("fcs_pb", latest)[order(-est)][!is.na(est)]
top3 <- reg_fcs_latest[1:3]
both_latest <- both_nat[round_id == latest]
worse <- pb(last_oct) > pb(first_oct) && pb(last_feb) > pb(first_feb)
p3_low <- rcsi_nat[weighted == TRUE][which.min(est_rcsi_p3)]
```

- **`r if (worse) "Food consumption deteriorated over the period." else "Food consumption trends."`** In October, the share of households with poor or borderline food consumption (FCS 28/42) `r dir_word(pb(first_oct), pb(last_oct))` from `r pct(pb(first_oct))`% in `r lab(first_oct)` to `r pct(pb(last_oct))`% in `r lab(last_oct)`, peaking at `r pct(peak_oct$est_fcs_pb)`% in `r peak_oct$round_lab`. In February it went from `r pct(pb(first_feb))`% (`r lab(first_feb)`) to `r pct(pb(last_feb))`% (`r lab(last_feb)`).
- **Severe consumption-based coping concerns a minority of households.** The share in rCSI phase 3 or above (rCSI ≥ 19) ranged from `r pct(min(rcsi_nat$est_rcsi_p3))`% to `r pct(max(rcsi_nat$est_rcsi_p3))`% across rounds. It was `r pct(p3(last_oct))`% in `r lab(last_oct)`, against `r pct(p3(first_oct))`% in `r lab(first_oct)` and a low of `r pct(p3_low$est_rcsi_p3)`% in `r p3_low$round_lab`.
- **Livelihood coping.** Using the strategies asked in every round, `r pct(g(lcs_nat, "est_lcs_ce", latest))`% of households resorted to crisis or emergency strategies in `r lab(latest)`, against `r pct(g(lcs_nat, "est_lcs_ce", first_oct))`% in `r lab(first_oct)` (range `r pct(min(lcs_nat$est_lcs_ce))`–`r pct(max(lcs_nat$est_lcs_ce))`% across rounds).
- **Hunger.** On the Household Hunger Scale, `r pct(g(hhs_nat, "est_hhs_p3", latest))`% of households were in phase 3 or above in `r lab(latest)`, against `r pct(g(hhs_nat, "est_hhs_p3", hhs_first_oct))`% in `r lab(hhs_first_oct)`; the highest share was `r pct(max(hhs_nat$est_hhs_p3))`% (`r hhs_nat[which.max(est_hhs_p3), round_lab]`). Severe hunger (score 4–6) stays below `r pct(max(hhs_nat$est_hhs_severe) + 0.005, 0)`% in every round.
- **Hotspots in `r lab(latest)`:** `r paste0(top3$admin1, " (", pct(top3$est, 0), "%)", collapse = ", ")` have the highest shares of poor or borderline consumption.
- **Overlap of the two dimensions:** in `r lab(latest)`, `r pct(both_latest$est)`% of households combined poor or borderline consumption with rCSI phase 3+.
- **Caveat:** `r paste(unweighted, collapse = ", ")` have no usable sampling weight and are estimated unweighted (marked †); February and October rounds reflect different seasons and should be compared within season.

# Data and methods

## Data

The analysis uses the harmonised household files produced by the ENSA harmonisation pipeline: `ensa_core` (keys, region, weight), `ensa_fcs` and `ensa_rcsi`, merged one-to-one on the household identifier. Together they cover `r int(nrow(d))` households in `r nrow(R)` rounds (Table \@ref(tab:rounds)).

```{r rounds}
t1 <- R[, .(round_id, round_lab, generation)]
t1 <- merge(t1, d[, .(households = .N, regions = uniqueN(admin1, na.rm = TRUE)), by = round_id], by = "round_id")
t1 <- merge(t1, cfg_rounds[, .(round_id, fieldwork = paste(format(as.Date(fieldwork_start), "%d %b"), "–",
                                                           format(as.Date(fieldwork_end), "%d %b %Y")))], by = "round_id")
t1 <- t1[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
t1[, weight := ifelse(round_id %in% R[weighted == TRUE, round_id], "survey weight", "none (unweighted †)")]
save_tab(t1, "T01_rounds")
ft(t1[, .(round_lab, generation, households = int(households), regions, fieldwork, weight)],
   header = list(round_lab = "Round", generation = "Questionnaire generation", households = "Households",
                 regions = "Regions", fieldwork = "Fieldwork", weight = "Weighting")) |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines("Fieldwork = 1st–99th percentile of interview dates. † No usable sampling weight in the source file.") |>
  cap("Survey rounds analysed", "rounds")
```

## Indicators

- **Food Consumption Score (FCS)** — days of consumption of 9 food groups over the last 7 days, weighted (staples 2, pulses 3, vegetables 1, fruit 1, meat/fish/eggs 4, dairy 4, sugar 0.5, oil 0.5, condiments 0). Groups: poor ≤ 28, borderline 28.5–42, acceptable > 42 (Chad thresholds); the 21/35 thresholds are shown for sensitivity.
- **Reduced Coping Strategies Index (rCSI)** — days of use of 5 strategies over the last 7 days, weighted (1, 2, 1, 3, 1); range 0–56. Cadre Harmonisé phases: phase 1 ≤ 3, phase 2 = 4–18, phase 3+ ≥ 19.
- **Household Dietary Diversity Score (HDDS)** — number of 12 food groups eaten by the household in the past 24 hours (0–12). Cadre Harmonisé phases: 5 groups or more → 1, 4 → 2, 3 → 3, 2 → 4, 0–1 → 5. In October 2024, questions on food groups not eaten in the past 7 days were skipped; they are counted as not eaten.
- **Household Hunger Scale (HHS)** — three questions on the past 30 days (no food in the house, went to sleep hungry, a whole day and night without eating), each scored 0 (never), 1 (rarely or sometimes) or 2 (often); score 0–6. WFP categories: little or none (0–1), moderate (2–3), severe (4–6). IPC / Cadre Harmonisé phases: 0 → 1, 1 → 2, 2–3 → 3, 4 → 4, 5–6 → 5. Collected from October 2019.
- **Livelihood Coping Strategies (LCS)** — strategies used in the past 30 days because of a lack of food (answer "yes" or "no, already exhausted"); each household is classified by the most severe strategy used (none, stress, crisis, emergency). The list of strategies and their severities changed between questionnaires, so the **comparable** indicator uses the 7 strategies asked in all rounds with a fixed severity (stress: sold household assets, sold more animals, spent savings; crisis: sold productive assets; emergency: sold house or land, sold last female animals, begged). From October 2024 the module covers coping for any essential need; only coping to buy food is counted, as in earlier rounds.

Both indicators were recomputed from the item answers with the same formula in every round; they agree with the scores computed by the original analysts in 98.7–100% of households (see the harmonisation documentation).

## Estimation

Estimates are survey-weighted (normalised weights, mean 1 within each round) with 95% confidence intervals from the `survey` package. `r if (params$cluster == "admin3") "The harmonised files do not carry the official strata and primary sampling units; sub-prefectures are used as approximate clusters, which gives conservative (wider) intervals." else "Confidence intervals assume simple random sampling and are therefore too narrow."` Regional estimates based on fewer than `r params$min_cell` households are suppressed. Regional changes compare `r lab(latest)` with `r lab(previous)`, the two most recent weighted October rounds.

# Sample and design (core domain)

```{r sample-calc}
n_round <- d[, .N, by = round_id]
```

The sample ranged from `r int(min(n_round$N))` households (`r lab(n_round[which.min(N), round_id])`) to `r int(max(n_round$N))` (`r lab(n_round[which.max(N), round_id])`); the largest samples, in 2024, include refugee and returnee strata (Figure \@ref(fig:sample)). Three questionnaire generations were used; harmonisation makes their indicators comparable.

```{r sample, fig.id = "sample", fig.cap = "Households interviewed per round, by questionnaire generation", fig.height = 3.4}
s <- d[, .N, by = .(round_lab, generation)]
p <- ggplot(s, aes(round_lab, N, fill = factor(generation))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = int(N)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL$gen, labels = GEN_LABEL, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Households", caption = "† No usable sampling weight.") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))
save_fig(p, "F01_sample", height = 3.4)
```

# Food consumption (FCS domain)

```{r fcs-text}
mean_first <- g(fcs_nat, "est_FCS", first_oct); mean_last <- g(fcs_nat, "est_FCS", last_oct)
```

The mean Food Consumption Score in October went from `r num(mean_first)` (`r lab(first_oct)`) to `r num(mean_last)` (`r lab(last_oct)`). Table \@ref(tab:fcs-national) gives the national estimates for every round and Figure \@ref(fig:fcs-groups) the distribution of households across the three consumption groups. The threshold choice matters: with the 21/35 thresholds, fewer households fall into the poor or borderline groups, but the trend is the same.

```{r fcs-national}
t2 <- fcs_nat[, .(Round = round_lab,
                  `Mean FCS` = num(est_FCS), `95% CI` = ci(lo_FCS, hi_FCS, scale = 1),
                  `Poor (%)` = pct(est_fcs_poor), `Borderline (%)` = pct(est_fcs_border),
                  `Acceptable (%)` = pct(est_fcs_accept),
                  `Poor + borderline (%)` = pct(est_fcs_pb), `95% CI ` = ci(lo_fcs_pb, hi_fcs_pb),
                  `P + B, 21/35 (%)` = pct(est_fcs_pb21))]
save_tab(fcs_nat, "T02_fcs_national")
ft(t2) |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines("Groups with the 28/42 thresholds unless stated. † Unweighted estimate (no sampling weight).") |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  cap("Food Consumption Score by round (national, 95% CI)", "fcs-national")
```

```{r fcs-groups, fig.id = "fcs-groups", fig.cap = "Households by FCS group (28/42), by round and season", fig.height = 3.8}
x <- melt(fcs_nat[, .(round_lab, season, Poor = est_fcs_poor, Borderline = est_fcs_border, Acceptable = est_fcs_accept)],
          id.vars = c("round_lab", "season"), variable.name = "group", value.name = "share")
x[, season := factor(season, c("Feb", "Oct"), c("February rounds", "October rounds"))]
x[, group := factor(group, levels = c("Acceptable", "Borderline", "Poor"))]
p <- ggplot(x, aes(round_lab, share, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(share >= 0.04, pct(share, 0), "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 2.5, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  facet_grid(~season, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL$fcs, name = NULL, breaks = c("Poor", "Borderline", "Acceptable")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of households", caption = "† Unweighted estimate.") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
save_fig(p, "F02_fcs_groups", height = 3.8)
```

## Diet composition

```{r diet-calc}
fg <- weighted_grid(d, names(FCS_GROUPS), by = c("round_id", "round_lab"), min_n = 0)
fg <- melt(fg[, -"n"], id.vars = c("round_id", "round_lab"), variable.name = "item", value.name = "days")
fg[, group := factor(FCS_GROUPS[as.character(item)], levels = rev(FCS_GROUPS))]
# Change in mean FCS between the first and last October rounds, split by food group:
# contribution = FCS weight x change in mean days.
fcs_w <- c(FCSStap = 2, FCSPulse = 3, FCSVeg = 1, FCSFruit = 1, FCSPr = 4, FCSDairy = 4, FCSSugar = 0.5, FCSFat = 0.5, FCSCond = 0)
dec <- dcast(fg[round_id %in% c(first_oct, last_oct)], item + group ~ round_id, value.var = "days")
dec[, contrib := fcs_w[as.character(item)] * (get(last_oct) - get(first_oct))]
dec <- dec[order(contrib)]
total <- sum(dec$contrib)
big3 <- dec[order(-abs(contrib))][1:3]
almost_daily <- fg[round_id == last_oct & days >= 5.5, as.character(group)]
```

Figure \@ref(fig:food-groups) shows how many days per week households ate each food group. In `r lab(last_oct)`, `r paste(tolower(almost_daily), collapse = ", ")` were eaten on at least 5.5 days a week. Between `r lab(first_oct)` and `r lab(last_oct)`, the mean FCS `r if (total < 0) "fell" else "rose"` by `r num(abs(total))` points. The largest contributions came from `r paste0(tolower(big3$group), " (", sprintf("%+.1f", big3$contrib), ")", collapse = ", ")` (Figure \@ref(fig:fcs-decomp)): the groups with the highest weights in the score drive its trend.

```{r food-groups, fig.id = "food-groups", fig.cap = "Mean days of consumption per week, by food group and round (weighted)", fig.height = 3.6}
save_tab(dcast(fg, group ~ round_lab, value.var = "days"), "T03_food_group_days")
p <- ggplot(fg, aes(round_lab, group, fill = days)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = num(days)), size = 2.4, colour = ifelse(fg$days > 4.5, "white", PAL$ink)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4F1EA", high = PAL$teal, limits = c(0, 7), name = "Days / week") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "† Unweighted estimate.") +
  theme_report() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank(),
                         legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))
save_fig(p, "F03_food_group_days", height = 3.6)
```

```{r fcs-decomp, fig.id = "fcs-decomp", fig.cap = paste0("Contribution of each food group to the change in mean FCS, ", lab(first_oct), " to ", lab(last_oct)), fig.height = 3.2}
save_tab(dec, "T03b_fcs_change_decomposition")
dec[, group := factor(as.character(group), levels = as.character(group))]
p <- ggplot(dec, aes(contrib, group, fill = contrib < 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$muted) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(abs(contrib) < 0.05, "0.0", sprintf("%+.1f", contrib)),
                hjust = ifelse(contrib < 0, 1.15, -0.15)), size = 2.8, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL$fcs[["Poor"]], `FALSE` = PAL$fcs[["Acceptable"]]), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.25)) +
  labs(x = "FCS points (weight × change in mean days)", y = NULL,
       caption = sprintf("Total change: %+.1f points. Weighted means; condiments have weight 0.", total)) +
  theme_report() + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
save_fig(p, "F03b_fcs_change_decomposition", height = 3.2)
```

## Regional differences

```{r fcs-region-table}
a <- region_est("fcs_pb", latest); b <- region_est("fcs_pb", previous)
rt <- merge(a[, .(admin1, n = N, est, lo, hi)], b[, .(admin1, prev = est)], by = "admin1", all.x = TRUE)
rt[, change := 100 * (est - prev)]
rt <- rt[order(-est)]
save_tab(rt, "T04_fcs_region")
ft(rt[, .(Region = admin1, Households = int(n), `% P+B` = pct(est), `95% CI` = ci(lo, hi),
          `% P+B, previous` = pct(prev), `Change (pp)` = ifelse(is.na(change), "–", sprintf("%+.1f", change)))]) |>
  colour_change(rt$change) |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines(sprintf("P+B = poor + borderline (28/42). Previous = %s. pp = percentage points; red = increase > 5 pp, green = decrease > 5 pp.", lab(previous))) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  cap(paste0("Poor + borderline food consumption by region, ", lab(latest), " vs ", lab(previous)), "fcs-region")
```

# Dietary diversity (HDDS domain)

```{r hdds-calc}
hg <- weighted_grid(d, names(HDDS_GROUPS), by = c("round_id", "round_lab"), min_n = 0)
hg <- melt(hg[, -"n"], id.vars = c("round_id", "round_lab"), variable.name = "item", value.name = "share")
hg[, group := factor(HDDS_GROUPS[as.character(item)], levels = rev(HDDS_GROUPS))]
low_latest <- hg[round_id == latest][order(share)][1:3]
```

The Household Dietary Diversity Score counts the food groups the household ate the day before the interview. The mean HDDS was `r num(g(hdds_nat, "est_HDDS", latest))` groups in `r lab(latest)` (`r num(g(hdds_nat, "est_HDDS", first_oct))` in `r lab(first_oct)`), and `r pct(g(hdds_nat, "est_hdds_p3", latest))`% of households ate 3 groups or fewer (phase 3 or above; Table \@ref(tab:hdds-national), Figure \@ref(fig:hdds-phases)). The least consumed groups in `r lab(latest)` were `r paste0(tolower(low_latest$group), " (", pct(low_latest$share, 0), "%)", collapse = ", ")` (Figure \@ref(fig:hdds-groups)). The 24-hour HDDS and the 7-day FCS describe the same diet over different periods.

```{r hdds-national}
save_tab(hdds_nat, "T15_hdds_national")
ft(hdds_nat[, .(Round = round_lab, `Mean HDDS` = num(est_HDDS, 2), `95% CI` = ci(lo_HDDS, hi_HDDS, d = 2, scale = 1),
```

# Coping strategies (rCSI domain)

```{r rcsi-text}
str_latest <- weighted_grid(d[round_id == latest], paste0("use_", names(RCSI_STRATEGIES)), by = "round_id", min_n = 0)
top_str <- names(which.max(unlist(str_latest[, -c("round_id", "n")])))
```

Table \@ref(tab:rcsi-national) and Figure \@ref(fig:rcsi-phases) show the rCSI and its Cadre Harmonisé phases. Most households fall in phases 1 and 2; phase 3+ (rCSI ≥ 19) concerns a minority but is the most relevant signal for food insecurity classification. The most common strategy in `r lab(latest)` was "`r tolower(RCSI_STRATEGIES[sub("use_", "", top_str)])`" (Figure \@ref(fig:strategies)).


# Livelihood coping strategies (LCS domain)

```{r lcs-calc}
lcs_use <- weighted_grid(d, paste0("use_", names(LCS_STRATEGIES)), by = c("round_id", "round_lab"), min_n = 0)
lcs_use <- melt(lcs_use[, -"n"], id.vars = c("round_id", "round_lab"), variable.name = "strategy", value.name = "share")
lcs_use[, item := sub("use_", "", strategy)]
top_lcs <- lcs_use[round_id == latest & !is.na(share)][order(-share)][1:3]
gap <- lcs_nat[round_id == latest, est_lcs_ce_round - est_lcs_ce]
```

Livelihood coping strategies show how households protect food consumption by drawing on their assets and future capacity. On the comparable indicator, `r pct(g(lcs_nat, "est_lcs_ce", latest))`% of households used crisis or emergency strategies in `r lab(latest)` (Table \@ref(tab:lcs-national), Figure \@ref(fig:lcs-cat)). The round-specific indicator, which uses all the strategies asked in that round, gives `r pct(g(lcs_nat, "est_lcs_ce_round", latest))`%: the difference (`r sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * gap)` points) comes from the strategies that are not asked in every round`r if (latest %in% c("2024-10", "2025-10")) " and from coping for non-food needs, which the round-specific indicator includes" else ""`. The most common strategies in `r lab(latest)` were `r paste0(tolower(LCS_STRATEGIES[top_lcs$item]), " (", pct(top_lcs$share, 0), "%)", collapse = ", ")` (Figure \@ref(fig:lcs-use)).

```{r lcs-national}

ft(lcs_nat[, .(Round = round_lab, `No strategy (%)` = pct(est_lcs_none), `Stress (%)` = pct(est_lcs_stress),
               `Crisis (%)` = pct(est_lcs_crisis), `Emergency (%)` = pct(est_lcs_emergency),
               `Crisis + emergency (%)` = pct(est_lcs_ce), `95% CI` = ci(lo_lcs_ce, hi_lcs_ce),
               `C + E, round-specific (%)` = pct(est_lcs_ce_round))]) |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines("Comparable indicator: 7 strategies asked in all rounds, fixed severity, coping for food only. Round-specific: all strategies asked in the round, with that round's severity. † Unweighted estimate.") |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  cap("Livelihood coping strategies: maximum category by round (national, 95% CI)", "lcs-national")
```

# Household Hunger Scale (HHS domain)

```{r hhs-calc}
hhs_q <- weighted_grid(d[!is.na(HHS)], names(HHS_QUESTIONS), by = c("round_id", "round_lab"), min_n = 0)
hhs_q <- melt(hhs_q[, -"n"], id.vars = c("round_id", "round_lab"), variable.name = "q", value.name = "share")
hhs_q[, question := factor(HHS_QUESTIONS[as.character(q)], levels = HHS_QUESTIONS)]
q_latest <- hhs_q[round_id == latest][order(-share)]
```

The Household Hunger Scale measures the most severe experience of food deprivation. It has been collected since `r lab(hhs_first_oct)`. In `r lab(latest)`, `r pct(g(hhs_nat, "est_hhs_p3", latest))`% of households were in phase 3 or above (score 2 or more), mostly with moderate hunger; severe hunger concerned `r pct(g(hhs_nat, "est_hhs_severe", latest))`% (Table \@ref(tab:hhs-national), Figure \@ref(fig:hhs-phases)). The most frequent experience was "`r tolower(q_latest$question[1])`" (`r pct(q_latest$share[1], 0)`% of households), the least frequent "`r tolower(q_latest$question[3])`" (`r pct(q_latest$share[3], 0)`%; Figure \@ref(fig:hhs-questions)).

```{r hhs-national}
  cap("Household Hunger Scale by round (national, 95% CI)", "hhs-national")
```

# Food consumption and coping combined

```{r combined-calc}
rho <- corr_by_round(d, "FCS", "rCSI")
strength <- function(r) if (max(abs(r)) < 0.3) "weak" else if (max(abs(r)) < 0.5) "weak to moderate" else "moderate to strong"
```

Merging the two domains shows how far they overlap. Households with lower food consumption tend to cope more, but the two indicators capture different dimensions: the rank correlation between FCS and rCSI is `r if (all(rho$rho < 0)) "negative" else "mostly negative"` and `r strength(rho$rho)` in every round (ρ between `r num(max(rho$rho), 2)` and `r num(min(rho$rho), 2)`; Table \@ref(tab:combined)). Few households combine both severe signals.

```{r combined}
cb <- merge(both_nat[, .(round_id, est, lo, hi)], rho, by = "round_id")
cb <- merge(R[, .(round_id, round_lab)], cb, by = "round_id")[order(match(round_id, R$round_id))]
save_tab(cb, "T09_combined")
ft(cb[, .(Round = round_lab, `P+B FCS and rCSI phase 3+ (%)` = pct(est), `95% CI` = ci(lo, hi),
          `Spearman ρ (FCS, rCSI)` = num(rho, 2))]) |>
  flextable::add_footer_lines("P+B = poor or borderline FCS (28/42). ρ < 0: lower consumption goes with more coping. † Unweighted estimate.") |>
  cap("Overlap of food consumption and coping, by round", "combined")
```

```{r joint, fig.id = "joint", fig.cap = paste0("Joint distribution of FCS group and rCSI phase, ", lab(latest), " (% of households, weighted)"), fig.height = 3}
save_tab(j, "T10_joint_latest")
p <- ggplot(j, aes(ch, fcs, fill = share)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct(share), "%")), size = 3.2, colour = ifelse(j$share > 0.25, "white", PAL$ink)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F4F1EA", high = PAL$navy, labels = scales::label_percent(), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "rCSI phase (Cadre Harmonisé)", y = "FCS group (28/42)") +
  theme_report() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
save_fig(p, "F08_joint_latest", height = 3)
```

```{r scatter, fig.id = "scatter", fig.cap = paste0("Regions by poor + borderline FCS and rCSI phase 3+, ", lab(latest)), fig.height = 4.4}
            region_est("rcsi_p3", latest)[, .(admin1, rcsi = est)], by = "admin1")[!is.na(fcs) & !is.na(rcsi)]

save_fig(p, "F09_region_scatter", height = 4.4)
```

# Limitations

- **Seasonality.** February (post-harvest) and October (harvest, end of the lean season) rounds are not directly comparable; trends should be read within season.
- **Weights.** `r paste(unweighted, collapse = ", ")` have no usable sampling weight; their estimates are unweighted and may be biased, particularly in 2024 when refugee and returnee strata were over-sampled.
- **Variance.** Confidence intervals use `r if (params$cluster == "admin3") "sub-prefectures as approximate clusters" else "simple random sampling"`, not the official sampling design.
- **Questionnaire changes.** Indicators were recomputed with identical formulas, but question wording and food-group examples changed between generations; small level shifts at the 2021 and 2023 generation changes cannot be ruled out.
- **Livelihood coping.** The comparable LCS indicator rests on 7 strategies with only one crisis strategy, so it understates crisis coping compared with the full module; use the round-specific indicator for a single round and the comparable one for trends. From October 2024 the module asks about coping for any essential need, then the reason; households that coped only for non-food needs are excluded from the comparable indicator.
- **Preliminary.** These are harmonised estimates for methodological review, not official ENSA results.
